context: Give the fallback one home. Export a single resolver from benchbox/mcp/schemas.py -- resolve_platform_policy_key(platform) -> str -- and have both validate_platform_options and _prepare_adapter_platform_options call it, so the rule can only ever be changed in one place. Keep the CONDITIONAL form as the surviving semantic: allow-list membership must win over suffix stripping, otherwise a future 'foo-df' entry could never have its own policy at all. Then pin it: a test that inserts a '-df'-suffixed key into the allow-list and asserts both call sites resolve to that key rather than to its base. Note the sequencing against one-engine-mcp-run-service-adoption, whose rung 1 deletes _prepare_adapter_platform_options -- if that lands first, the second call site moves and this item must be re-pointed at wherever option translation ends up; the resolver in schemas.py survives either way, which is why it is the right place to put it.
description:
The MCP option layer decides twice which platform's policy a '-df' request falls back to, using two different rules:

  benchbox/mcp/schemas.py:513   if platform_name not in MCP_PLATFORM_OPTION_ALLOWLIST and platform_name.endswith('-df'):
                                    policy_name = platform_name[:-3]      <- CONDITIONAL strip
  benchbox/mcp/tools/benchmark.py:101   platform_name = platform.lower().removesuffix('-df')   <- UNCONDITIONAL strip

Admission strips '-df' only when the full name is absent from the allow-list; preparation strips it always. The two agree today for exactly one reason: no key in MCP_PLATFORM_OPTION_ALLOWLIST ends in '-df'. Nothing states that, and nothing tests it. Add a '-df'-suffixed allow-list key -- a plausible thing to do when a dataframe surface needs options its SQL sibling does not -- and admission validates against that key's own specs, contract matrix and cross-field rules while preparation translates using the BASE platform's rules. That is the 'schema half closed, adapter half open' shape the whole mcp-v2 batch existed to close, sitting one allow-list entry away.

Not exploitable today and not a latent bug in current behaviour; it is an unstated coincidence guarding the exact defect class. Verified still present on develop bc5f2b0f4a.

Identified 2026-08-04 during the adversarial review of the mcp-v2-platform-options batch. It was the one review finding that did not make it into an item at the time; the three nits in mcp-option-policy-hardening-nits are log amplification, bare asserts under -O, and the duplicate profile-name regex -- not this.

anti_patterns.dont: close this by adding a test that merely asserts the two expressions produce equal results for today's platform names
anti_patterns.instead: delete one of the two expressions, and pin the survivor with a case that actually inserts a '-df'-suffixed allow-list key
anti_patterns.why: that pins the coincidence rather than removing it: it passes for every current name and still passes on the day someone adds a '-df' allow-list key, because the test never exercises one

anti_patterns.dont: leave the second call site in place with a comment saying it must be kept in sync
anti_patterns.instead: one exported resolver, two callers, no second expression
anti_patterns.why: a comment is not an invariant; the duplicated ClickHouse/DuckDB/Databricks halves this batch fixed were all documented and still drifted

anti_patterns.dont: make admission unconditional to match preparation, since that is the smaller diff
anti_patterns.instead: keep the conditional form -- allow-list membership wins over suffix stripping -- and make preparation adopt it
anti_patterns.why: it would permanently prevent any '-df' platform from carrying its own option policy, silently routing a future dataframe surface's options through its SQL sibling's rules

preserves.behavior: Current resolution for every platform name in use today is byte-for-byte unchanged: no allow-list key ends in '-df', so the conditional and unconditional rules already agree and must keep agreeing
clickhouse-df still inherits the clickhouse cross-field policy, including the deployment_mode='server' requirement for a connection profile
validate_platform_options remains the single admission chokepoint reached by sync run_benchmark, durable start_benchmark, and durable worker replay

prior_art.concept: the conditional policy-key fallback added during #1510 after the clickhouse-df alias was found bypassing the new cross-field rules
the unconditional removesuffix that is the second, independent copy of the same decision
test_dataframe_alias_fallback_does_not_bypass_the_policy already covers the clickhouse-df case from the admission side only
